thread:
maya: Heads up — saw a ~7% jump in `kv_occupancy_p99` for the long-context cohort around 03:12 UTC. Anyone else seeing correlated evictions or weird memory growth?

tariq: Which exact metric / label set? screenshot or query pls.

maya: The panel is `redwood_kv_occupancy_percentiles{cohort="long-context",quantile="0.99"}` on the kv-observability board. Link: https://grafana/internal/d/kv/kv-observability (private). Spike aligns with a burst of long-session traffic.

dashbot: runtime-deploy-bot: No active deploys at 03:00-03:20 UTC.

olivia: Pulled the eviction counts for that window. Quick prom query I ran:
```
sum by (cohort,reason) (increase(redwood_kv_eviction_total{job="runtime"}[5m]))
```
Result: long-context had a jump in `reason="compact"` and small bump in `reason="age"`.

sam: Hmm — occupancy up but residency percentiles for the same cohort look flat. That smells like fragmentation + reduced reuse, not aggressive eviction.

maya: Agreed. If residency stable but occupancy grows, we might be leaking page chains or not coalescing fragments effectively. Any `kv_page_chain_*` metrics?

olivia: Yes — saw `kv_page_chain_length_avg{cohort="long-context"}` increase from 1.8 -> 3.4 at the same time. Prom query: `avg_over_time(kv_page_chain_length_avg{cohort="long-context"}[10m])`.

sam: That supports fragmentation. Also check `kv_fragment_count` and `kv_fragment_reuse_ratio`. We currently only export global reuse ratio; we should break it out by cohort.

maya: Good ask. We only have cohort-level occupancy percentiles and eviction totals. Proposal: export `redwood_kv_fragment_count{cohort}`, `redwood_kv_fragment_reuse_ratio{cohort}`, and `redwood_kv_occupancy_bytes_by_cohort`.

tariq: I'll add a Grafana panel for `occupancy bytes by cohort` and a simple alert: when p95 occupancy > 60% AND increase(occupancy_p95[5m]) > 8% for two consecutive windows. Is that too sensitive?

olivia: Might be noisy on heavy traffic days. Suggest coupling with `increase(redwood_kv_eviction_total[5m]) > 0` to avoid false positives on normal traffic fluctuations.

sam: Also recommend a derived alert for fragmentation: `kv_fragment_count` growth > 30% combined with `fragment_reuse_ratio` drop > 10% over 10m. That would point to poor coalescing.

maya: Can we also instrument an `evictions_per_active_session` gauge so we can normalize by session concurrency? Right now absolute evictions are hard to interpret.

tariq: Good idea. I can add a prometheus recording rule: `rate_evictions_per_active_session = increase(redwood_kv_eviction_total[5m]) / max(1, avg_over_time(runtime_active_sessions[5m]))` and surface that.

olivia: For immediate triage, I dumped a small heap profile and KV fragment map from one box at 03:13. Uploaded to the shared folder: gs://redwood-debug/kv/03-12-longcontext-sample.tgz

sam: Will inspect the fragment map later today. Early glance: several >128KB small fragments scattered across 3 slabs — explains page chain growth.

maya: Short-term mitigation: lower coalescing threshold is risky but might reduce fragmentation. Long-term: fix the slab allocator hotspots + add cohort-aware compaction.

tariq: I'll schedule the dashboard updates and the new recording rules. Olivia, can you add the cohort-level fragment/export metrics to the runtime PR?

olivia: Yep — I'll open a draft PR with metric names and example queries.

maya: Thanks. Can we add a small playbook note to `eng-runtime/ops-runbook` describing steps if occupancy p95 crosses 65% and eviction_per_session rises? Quick checklist: 1) verify deploys 2) check fragment_count/reuse 3) grab profile & fragment map 4) consider temporary coalescing tweak.

sam: +1. I'll add a short entry.

tariq: Will follow up here when panels/alerts live.

maya: Great. Thanks all :thumbsup:

dashbot: Note: Incident channel crosspost prepared if alert fires after rollout.
